title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The Cid kneels before Alfonso and is pardoned (tirada 104, second part, lines 2013–2067)
part: Tirada 104 (second part) · The Cid kneels before Alfonso and is pardoned (lines 2013–2067)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 255–258, lines 2013–2067 (tiradas 104–104). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.t: De un día es llegado antes el rey don Alfons.
sentences.l: By one day has arrived before the king don Alfons.
sentences.i: King Alfonso has arrived a day ahead.
sentences.n: Tirada 104 continued (assonance ó) — the king and the Çid meet on the banks of the Tajo; the solemn pardon; the feasting (Pidal's rubric, the part of it that falls here: El rey y el Cid se avistan a orillas del Tajo.—Perdón solemne dado por el rey al Cid.—Convites). The tirada and its stressed ó at the line-end (Alfons, Campeador, onor, naçió) run on from the previous part, which ended at v. 2012 with the Çid on the road. De un día … antes, 'by one day … before': the king has come a day early to the meeting-place, as he will say himself at v. 2048. es llegado, 'is arrived', the perfect of a verb of motion made with ser, not aver. Alfons, the short form of Alfonsso.

sentences.t:
Quando vieron que vinie el buen Campeador,
reçebir lo salen con tan grand onor.
sentences.l:
When they-saw that was-coming the good Campeador,
to-receive him they-go-out with so great honour.
sentences.i: When they saw that the good Campeador was coming, they rode out to receive him with such great honour.
sentences.n: vinie = venía, imperfect in -ie. The subject of vieron and salen is the king's people. reçebir lo salen, 'they go out to receive him': the pronoun stands loose between the infinitive and the verb that governs it. onor here is the honour shown him, the ceremony of the welcome (con tan grand onor, 'with such great honour'), not the 'estate, lordship' the house gives it where it is held or lost (la onor, tirada 102): one does not receive a man 'with an estate'. So 'honour' in both lines here; ondra, the honour a man has, is another word. The preterite vieron and the present salen side by side: the epic tense-mixing.

sentences.t:
Don lo ovo a ojo el que en buen ora naçió,
a todos los sos estar los mandó,
si non a estos cavalleros que querie de coraçón.
sentences.l:
Where him he-had at eye he who in good hour was-born,
to all the his to-stop them he-ordered,
except to these knights whom he-loved from heart.
sentences.i: As soon as he who was born in a good hour caught sight of him, he ordered all his men to halt, except those knights he loved with all his heart.
sentences.n: Don = donde, here of time, 'when, as soon as' (as in Don llegan los otros, tirada 83). lo ovo a ojo, 'had him in eye', caught sight of him: aver 'to have, hold' as a full verb; lo is the king. el que en buen ora naçió, 'he who was born in a good hour', the formula. Pidal's note: estar, 'detenerse, quedarse quieto', 'to halt, stay still'. a todos los sos … los: the men are named with a and taken up again by los. sos = sus. si non, 'except'. querie = quería, imperfect in -ie; de coraçón, 'from the heart'.

sentences.t:
Con unos quinze a tierras firió,
commo lo comidía el que en buen ora naçió;
sentences.l:
With some fifteen to lands he-struck,
as it he-was-intending he who in good hour was-born;
sentences.i: With some fifteen of them he dismounted, as he who was born in a good hour had planned it;
sentences.n: Pidal's note: a tierras firió, 'echó pie a tierra', 'set foot to the ground', dismounted (compare v. 1842); firió, preterite of ferir (= herir, 'to strike'), f- for modern h-. Pidal's note: comidía, 'como pensaba', 'como había dispuesto', 'as he had in mind, as he had arranged': imperfect of comedir, 'to consider, plan'. The Çid's abasement is premeditated, a public act of homage.

sentences.t:
los inojos e las manos en tierra los fincó,
las yerbas del campo a dientes las tomó,
llorando de los ojos, tanto avié el gozo mayor;
assí sabe dar omildança a Alfons so señor.
sentences.l:
the knees and the hands on ground them he-planted,
the grasses of-the field at teeth them he-took,
weeping from the eyes, so-much he-had the joy greater;
thus he-knows-how to-give homage to Alfons his lord.
sentences.i: he set his knees and his hands upon the ground and took the grass of the field between his teeth, weeping from his eyes, so great was his joy: such is the homage he knows how to pay to Alfonso, his lord.
sentences.n: los inojos … los fincó, las yerbas … las tomó: in both lines the object comes first and is taken up again by a pronoun. The print's los at the head of v. 2021 is damaged (its o is broken); los is the reading. inojos = hinojos, 'knees'; fincar = hincar, 'to plant, drive in' (f- for h-), as with Ximena kneeling before the Çid at Cardeña (fincó los inojos, v. 264). Pidal's note to v. 2022: 'mordió la yerba', 'he bit the grass'; he compares the classical phrase 'to bite the earth' ('to die, be defeated') and its German variant ins Gras beissen (printed Grans), 'to bite the grass', and cites G. L. Hamilton (The Romanic Review IV, 1913, pp. 226–227) for the custom, shown among Indic, Italic, Germanic and Slavic peoples, that the vanquished took grass in the mouth or in the hand in sign of submission or when begging mercy: the Cid's sign of surrender to the king is a survival of that custom. Llorando de los ojos, the poem's weeping formula. tanto avié el gozo mayor, 'so much did he have the greater joy', so great was his joy (avié = había). Pidal's note: omildança, 'acatamiento', 'reverence, homage'. sabe dar, present among the preterites: saber + infinitive, 'to know how to'. so = su.

sentences.t:
De aquesta guisa a los pie[de]s le cayó;
tan grand pesar ovo el rey don Alfons:
sentences.l:
Of this manner at the feet to-him he-fell;
so great grief had the king don Alfons:
sentences.i: In this way he fell at his feet; so great was the grief King Alfonso felt:
sentences.n: De aquesta guisa, 'in this manner' (aquesta = esta; guisa, 'way'). pie[de]s, the old plural piedes, 'feet', its de Pidal's (in italics), as elsewhere. le cayó, 'fell to him', at his feet. tan grand pesar ovo, 'such great sorrow he had': the king is pained to see his vassal so low, and says so at once.

sentences.i: “Rise to your feet, Çid Campeador; kiss my hands, but not my feet. If you do not do this, you will not have my favour.”
sentences.n: Levantados = levantad + (v)os, 'raise yourself', the imperative with the pronoun fastened on and the v of vos lost after the -d. ya Çid, 'O Çid' (ya, the calling particle). ca, 'for': 'kiss the hands, for (you should kiss) not the feet'. pie[de]s again, de Pidal's. feches, present of fer (= hacéis), 'you do'. avredes, future of aver, 'you will have'. amor, the lord's love for his vassal: 'favour' in the English. The threat is affectionate: the king will not accept homage so abject.

sentences.t:
Hinojos fitos sedie el Campeador:
“¡Merçed vos pido a vos, mio natural señor,
assí estando, dédesme vuestra amor,
que lo oyan [todos] quantos aquí son.”
sentences.l:
Knees fixed was-sitting the Campeador:
“Mercy to-you I-ask of you, my natural lord,
thus being, give-me your love,
that it they-may-hear [all] as-many-as here are.”
sentences.i: The Campeador stayed on his knees: “I ask your mercy, my natural lord; as I kneel here, grant me your favour, so that all who are here may hear it.”
sentences.n: Hinojos fitos, 'knees fixed', kneeling: fito, 'fixed, planted' (Latin fictus), the old participle that goes with fincar 'to plant': an absolute phrase (here Hinojos with h-, inojos at v. 2021: the print's inconsistency kept). sedie = seía, imperfect of seer, 'to sit, be'. Merçed vos pido a vos, the pronoun said twice, vos … a vos, for emphasis. Pidal prints the opening ¡ but no closing ! (the speech runs on with a comma); kept as printed. mio natural señor, 'my natural lord', the lord to whom one is bound by birth. assí estando, 'being thus', on my knees: he will rise only when pardoned. dédesme = dedes + me, present subjunctive of dar (= deis), a request, 'give me'. vuestra amor: amor is feminine here (mi, v. 2029, does not show the gender). oyan, subjunctive of oír. [todos], the whole word Pidal's (in italics); he gives no note on it. The line is numbered 2032b in Pidal. The pardon must be public: this is the point of the meeting.

sentences.i: The king said: “This I will do with all my heart and soul: here I pardon you and give you my favour, and from this day a place in all my kingdom.”
sentences.n: feré, future of fer (= haré). d'alma e de coraçón, 'from soul and from heart', the apostrophe as printed. dovos = do + vos, 'I give you' (do = doy). Pidal's note to v. 2035: dovos en todo mio reyno parte, 'os doy acogida en mi reino', 'I give you welcome, a footing, in my kingdom' (compare vv. 1938, 2363): parte, 'share, place', the exile's right to be received in the realm again. ên = e + en, 'and in': Pidal's circumflex marks two words run together, as in lâ (v. 914), lês (v. 975), mê (v. 1029) and âquel (v. 1222); his footnote, which joins dovos to en todo mio reyno parte, fits this. The circumflex is clear on the scan. desde oy, 'from today'.

sentences.t:
Fabló mio Çid e dixo [esta razón]:
“merced; yo lo reçibo, Alfons mio señor;
gradéscolo a Dios del çielo e después a vos,
e a estas mesnadas que están a derredor.”
sentences.l:
Spoke my Çid and said [this speech]:
“mercy; I it receive, Alfons my lord;
I-thank-it to God of-the heaven and after to you,
and to these companies that are around.”
sentences.i: My Çid spoke and said these words: “Thank you; I receive it, Alfonso, my lord. I give thanks for it to God in heaven, and after him to you, and to these companies standing round about.”
sentences.n: [esta razón], both words Pidal's (in italics), no note: the formula Fabló mio Çid e dixo esta razón, which the manuscript gives whole at v. 2043. razón, 'speech, words'. merced, 'thank you', here as an exclamation of gratitude, printed with plain c (merçed at v. 2031); kept as printed. The next line is numbered 2036b in Pidal. gradéscolo = gradesco + lo, 'I am grateful for it' (gradeçer = agradecer). después, 'afterwards, next'. mesnadas, the companies of armed retainers, the king's and his own. a derredor, 'round about'.

sentences.t:
Hinojos fitos las manos le besó.
Levós en pie e en la bócal saludó.
sentences.l:
Knees fixed the hands to-him he-kissed.
He-raised-himself on foot and on the mouth-him he-greeted.
sentences.i: Still kneeling, he kissed the king's hands; then he rose to his feet and kissed him on the mouth in greeting.
sentences.n: Hinojos fitos, kneeling, as at v. 2030: now that he is pardoned, he does what the king asked at v. 2028. Levós = levóse, 'raised himself'. Pidal's note to v. 2040: 'levantóse en pie y le besó en la boca', 'he rose to his feet and kissed him on the mouth' (compare v. 3030): saludar, 'to greet', here with the kiss of peace between lord and vassal. bócal = boca + l(e), 'the mouth (to) him': the pronoun le is squeezed to -l and fastened, unusually, to the noun before the verb.

sentences.t:
Todos los demás desto avien sabor;
pesó a Álbar Diaz e a Garci Ordóñez.
sentences.l:
All the others of-this had pleasure;
it-weighed to Álbar Diaz and to Garci Ordóñez.
sentences.i: All the others took pleasure in it; it weighed on Álvar Díaz and on Garci Ordóñez.
sentences.n: desto = de esto. avien sabor, 'had pleasure' (aver sabor de, 'to take pleasure in'), avien = habían. pesó a, 'it weighed on, grieved' (as pesó a Garci Ordóñez, v. 1345). Pidal's note: Albar Diaz, a potestad (a great lord) of the court of Alfonso VI and an enemy of the Cid (he refers to p. 23, in his introduction, where he calls him Álvar Díaz: at court between 1068 and 1111, often as governor of Oca, near Burgos). Diaz is printed without an accent; Álvar Díaz in the English, as Albar becomes Álvar. Garci Ordóñez is Count García, the Çid's old enemy at court (v. 1345; the co[m]de don Garcia of v. 1836). Ordóñez, stressed ó with the unstressed -ez disregarded, counts in the ó assonance.

sentences.t:
Fabló mio Çid e dixo esta razón:
“Esto gradesco al [padre] Criador,
quando he la graçia de Alfons mio señor;
valer me a Dios de día e de noch.
sentences.l:
Spoke my Çid and said this speech:
“This I-thank to-the [father] Creator,
when I-have the grace of Alfons my lord;
help me will God by day and by night.
sentences.i: My Çid spoke and said these words: “For this I give thanks to the Father, the Creator, now that I have the grace of Alfonso, my lord; God will help me by day and by night.
sentences.n: Here the formula has esta razón in the manuscript (compare the restoration at v. 2036). [padre], Pidal's (in italics): 'the Father Creator'; the line is numbered 2043b. gradesco = agradezco. quando, 'now that, since'. he = he (aver), 'I have'. valer me a = me valdrá, 'will help me': the split future, infinitive + pronoun + a (= ha), as dezir vos he, 'I will tell you'. Pidal's note: de día e de noch, 'siempre', 'always' (v. 222).

sentences.t: F[o]ssedes mi[o] huesped, si vos ploguiesse, señor.”
sentences.l: Were-you my guest, if to-you it-should-please, lord.”
sentences.i: Would you be my guest, my lord, if it pleased you?”
sentences.n: F[o]ssedes, imperfect subjunctive of seer (= fueseis), 'were you, would you were', a courteous wish; the o is Pidal's (in italics), and so is the o of mi[o]. huesped, 'guest'. ploguiesse, imperfect subjunctive of plazer, 'if it should please you'. The Çid, now restored to favour, offers the king hospitality.

sentences.t:
Dixo el rey: “non es aguisado oy:
vos agora llegastes, e nos viniemos anoch;
mio huesped seredes, Çid Campeador,
e cras feremos lo que ploguiere a vos.”
sentences.l:
Said the king: “not it-is fitting today:
you now arrived, and we came last-night;
my guest you-will-be, Çid Campeador,
and tomorrow we-will-do what may-please to you.”
sentences.i: The king said: “It is not fitting today: you have only just arrived, and we came yesterday; you shall be my guest, Çid Campeador, and tomorrow we will do as you please.”
sentences.n: aguisado, 'fitting, proper' (from guisa, 'way'). llegastes, preterite 2nd pl. (= llegasteis); viniemos = vinimos. Pidal's note: anoch, 'ayer', 'yesterday' (compare v. 2013, where the king arrived a day ahead; he refers to his Cantar, p. 293). The host is the one who arrived first. seredes, future of seer, 'you will be'. cras, 'tomorrow' (Latin cras). feremos, future of fer. ploguiere, future subjunctive of plazer, 'whatever may please'.

sentences.t: Besóle la mano mio Çid, lo otorgó.
sentences.l: Kissed-him the hand my Çid, it he-granted.
sentences.i: My Çid kissed his hand and agreed.
sentences.n: Besóle, 'kissed him (the hand)', le the person whose hand it is. otorgar, 'to grant, consent to'. No link between the two verbs.

sentences.t:
Essora se le omillan iffantes de Carrión:
“Omillámosnos, Çid, en buen[a] nasquiestes vos!
En quanto podemos andamos en vuestro pro.”
sentences.l:
Then themselves to-him bow infantes of Carrión:
“We-bow-ourselves, Çid, in good (hour) you-were-born you!
In as-much-as we-can we-go in your profit.”
sentences.i: Then the Infantes of Carrión bow before him: “We salute you, Çid — in a good hour were you born! As far as we can, we are working for your good.”
sentences.n: Essora, 'then, at that hour' (= entonces). Pidal's note: omillarse a uno, 'saludarle', 'to greet him' (compare v. 1396, Omillom, doña Ximena). iffantes de Carrión, the young lords of Carrión, the would-be bridegrooms (vv. 1372–77): this is their first word to the Çid. Omillámosnos = omillamos + nos, 'we humble ourselves'. en buen[a] nasquiestes vos, the birth-formula with ora left unsaid, the a Pidal's (as at v. 294). nasquiestes, preterite 2nd pl. of naçer. Pidal's note to v. 2054: 'somos vuestros buenos amigos', 'we are your good friends' (v. 1388): andar en pro de, 'to go about someone's advantage'. Their courtesy will not last.

sentences.t: Respuso mio Çid: “assí lo mande el Criador!”
sentences.l: Answered my Çid: “thus it may-command the Creator!”
sentences.i: My Çid answered: “May the Creator so ordain!”
sentences.n: Respuso, preterite of responder, 'answered'. mande, present subjunctive, a wish. A cautious reply: he leaves it to God.

sentences.t:
Mio Çid R[o]y Díaz, que en ora buena naçió,
en aquel día del rey so huesped f[o];
sentences.l:
My Çid Ruy Díaz, who in hour good was-born,
on that day of-the king his guest he-was;
sentences.i: My Çid Ruy Díaz, who was born in a good hour, was the king's guest that day;
sentences.n: R[o]y Díaz, Ruy Díaz, the o Pidal's (in italics). en ora buena naçió, the formula with its adjective after the noun. del rey so huesped, 'of the king his guest', the king's guest (so = su). f[o] = fue, 'was', the o Pidal's.

sentences.t:
non se puede fartar dél, tántol querie de coraçón:
catándol sedie la barba, que tan aínal creçi[ó].
sentences.l:
not himself he-can sate of-him, so-much-him he-loved from heart:
looking-at-him he-was-sitting the beard, which so quickly-to-him grew.
sentences.i: the king could not have enough of him, he loved him so dearly; he sat gazing at the Çid's beard, which had grown so long so soon.
sentences.n: The subject is the king. fartar = hartar, 'to sate' (f- for h-): non se puede fartar dél, 'he cannot get his fill of him'. tántol = tanto le. catándol = catándole, 'looking at him … the beard', the le of the person whose beard it is; sedie, 'sat, was' (seer + gerund, a continuing action). aínal = aína le, 'so quickly on him'; creçi[ó], the ó Pidal's. Pidal's note: tan aína, 'tan pronto', 'so soon': the Cid had not been long in exile, nor long under his vow not to cut his beard (v. 1241), and although he was always bien barbado (v. 789), his beard was now so grown that it amazed all who saw him (vv. 2059–60, 3273–74); hence the minstrel's epithets el de la luenga barba (v. 1226) and el de la barba grant (v. 2410).

sentences.t: Maravíllanse de mio Çid quantos que y son.
sentences.l: Marvel-themselves at my Çid as-many-as that there are.
sentences.i: All who are there marvel at my Çid.
sentences.n: Maravíllanse, 'they marvel' (maravillarse de). quantos que y son, 'as many as are there' (y = there; the que is pleonastic), as quantos que i son at v. 1998.

sentences.t: Es día es passado, e entrada es la noch.
sentences.l: That day is passed, and entered is the night.
sentences.i: That day is over, and night has come.
sentences.n: Es día = ese día, 'that day'. es passado, entrada es: perfects of intransitive verbs made with ser, as es llegado, v. 2013. noch = noche.

sentences.i: Next morning, as the sun rose bright, the Campeador ordered his men to make ready a feast for all who were there;
sentences.n: Otro día mañana, 'next day in the morning'. salie, imperfect, 'was rising'. a los sos lo mando: lo looks forward to the que clause; mando is printed so, without an accent (checked on an enlarged crop of p. 258), and Pidal has no note; we read the preterite mandó, which the sense and the ó assonance require. adobassen, imperfect subjunctive of adobar, 'to prepare'. cozina, 'cooking, cooked food': a meal. pora = para.

sentences.t:
de tal guisa los paga mio Çid el Campeador,
todos eran alegres e acuerdan en una razón:
passado avie tres años no comieran mejor.
sentences.l:
of such manner them pleases my Çid the Campeador,
all were glad and agree in one word:
passed had three years not they-had-eaten better.
sentences.i: My Çid the Campeador so contented them that they were all merry and agreed with one voice: not in three years had they eaten better.
sentences.n: pagar, 'to please, content' (compare de coraçón se paga, v. 1960): los paga, 'he satisfies them', present amid imperfects (eran, avie): the tense-mixing again. acuerdan en una razón, 'they agree in one speech', all say the same. passado avie tres años, 'three years had passed', avie impersonal; comieran, pluperfect in -ra, 'they had (not) eaten': not since three years had they fed so well. The first day of the meeting ends here; the king's request for the Çid's daughters comes next morning, after mass (v. 2068), in the next part.
